productionBoundary: AppSession already passes its current publication key ID. Reuse is restricted to that same requested key, namespace and generation; an explicitly different ready key retains the original deliberate key-rotation CSR path.

The Vault reopens the permanent Keychain key and fully authenticates the exact old publication at its acknowledged publication date solely to obtain an identity/expiry baseline. It then classifies bounded certificate DER times with the existing parser and separately requires the complete certificate chain to validate at the real current date against configured anchors without network fetching.

Only absent/different publication or explicitly expired chain dates mean no reusable certificate. Clock rollback, malformed old material, missing/revoked/mismatched key, storage failures, stale generations and other trust errors propagate. Historical profile verification grants no current signing lease.

The same real account/team checks and complete development-certificate-list request run before reuse. Its exact DER and public-key hash must match the Vault capability. Missing remote DER takes the existing CSR path and does not revoke any certificate.

Both reuse and CSR branches call the same extracted existing three-profile network loop. Account/team are rechecked after all profile awaits. Reuse publication reopens the key, rechecks generation and exact chain/baseline, validates every new profile at now through the original double-CMS/identity/leaf verifier, and requires each component expiry strictly advance.

Publication still uses the existing Vault publish/CAS/Keychain save. No post-commit cancellation check hides a successful publication. Reuse performs no CSR and needs no account-journal rewrite; pending unknown CSR is refused before selecting either branch, and existing issue/reconcile/finalization logic is byte-exact.
